title: Sync Channels and Backpressure
goal: Understand how bounded channels block senders when full.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Bounded Channels

sections.text: You use `mpsc::sync_channel` when you need backpressure between threads. Standard `mpsc::channel` is unbounded and grows until memory runs out.

sections.caption: sync_channel takes a maximum buffer capacity.

sections.text: When the buffer is full, calling `send` blocks the current thread until the receiver calls `recv` to clear space.
Passing zero creates a rendezvous channel where every `send` blocks immediately until a receiving thread calls `recv`.

sections.code:
let (tx, rx) = mpsc::sync_channel(0);
// tx.send(1) waits for rx.recv()
sections.caption: Zero capacity forces both threads to meet at the transfer point.

sections.text: Handling thread synchronization with async tasks uses a different channel type covered in the async deck later.

explanation: Understand how bounded channels block senders when full.
